items.en: Right, the chorus of your life just ended—here’s the bridge, and it’s wearing a monocle.
items.zh: 行，你人生的副歌唱完了——接下来是桥段，还戴了个单片眼镜。

items.en: Next up: a tune for when your toast lands butter-side down, yet you still salute the floor.
items.zh: 接下来这首歌，献给吐司黄油面着地、却依然向地板敬礼的你。

items.en: This one’s for the queue at 8 a.m. — brisk, sardonic, and slightly over-caffeinated.
items.zh: 这首献给早上八点排队的人——利落、刻薄，外加咖啡因上头。

items.en: A little something for the existential pause between “I should” and “I shan’t” — enjoy the wobble.
items.zh: 给“我应该”和“我偏不”之间的存在主义停顿来点小料——享受这摇摆吧。

items.en: And now, a melody for your imaginary dog that judges your Wi-Fi speed — trot on.
items.zh: 现在，献给你那只评判你Wi-Fi速度的假想狗一首曲子——快跑吧。

items.en: Well, if your Monday’s had a face, it’d be this next tune—slightly smudged, but oddly charming.
items.zh: 要是你的周一有张脸，那准是这首歌——有点糊，但怪招人喜欢的。

items.en: Here’s a song for when you’ve locked yourself out of your own life, but the locksmith’s on hold.
items.zh: 这首歌献给那些把自己锁在人生门外、而开锁师傅还在排队等接听的人。

items.en: This next one’s a bit like your last relationship—over before the chorus, but you hum it anyway.
items.zh: 下一首有点像你上一段感情——副歌没到就完了，但你还是会哼两句。

items.en: Up next: a little rhythm for that existential dread you’ve been cultivating—garden gloves not included.
items.zh: 接下来：给你那精心培育的存在主义焦虑来点小节奏——园艺手套可不在套餐里。

items.en: And now, the audio equivalent of a raised eyebrow in a crowded lift—enjoy the awkward.
items.zh: 现在，请欣赏电梯里人满为患时那声挑眉的音频版——好好享受这份尴尬吧。

items.en: Well, if your Monday had a pulse, this next tune’s gonna give it a proper little shake.
items.zh: 行，要是你周一还带点儿活气儿，这首歌准保给你抖搂精神了。

items.en: Ah, the sound of life’s remote control — someone’s just pressed “skip” on their own existential dread.
items.zh: 哎，人生的遥控器响了——有人刚按了“跳过”自己的存在主义焦虑。

items.en: This next bit of noise? It’s like a polite argument with your own heartbeat — and I think the heartbeat’s winning.
items.zh: 接下来的这段噪音？就像跟自己的心跳礼貌地吵一架——而且我觉得心跳快赢了。

items.en: For those of you stuck in traffic, consider this your musical middle finger to the universe — tasteful, of course.
items.zh: 堵在路上的各位，就当这是给宇宙的一根优雅中指吧——当然，得是那种有品位的。

items.en: Right, time to swap the kettle’s whistle for something with a bit more rhythm — brace your earlobes, dears.
items.zh: 行，该把水壶的哨声换成更有节奏的动静了——各位，耳朵可要绷紧点儿。

items.en: Well, if your Monday feels like a wet biscuit, this next tune’s the jam.
items.zh: 要是你的周一像块泡软的饼干，那这首歌就是救命的果酱。

items.en: Ah, the perfect soundtrack for pretending you’re a spy—until the kettle screams.
items.zh: 啊，假装自己是特工的完美配乐——直到水壶尖叫起来。

items.en: Right then, here’s a little sonic marmalade for your soggy toast of a day.
items.zh: 行，那就给你这湿哒哒的日子来点声音果酱吧。

items.en: This one’s for those moments you lock yourself out—and blame the universe.
items.zh: 这杯敬那些把自己锁在门外、还怪宇宙不公的时刻。

items.en: Behold, the musical equivalent of finding a fiver in last winter’s coat.
items.zh: 瞧，这简直是冬天大衣里翻出五块钱的音乐版。

items.en: Well, if your Monday had a face, I'd punch it—but here's music to numb the bruise.
items.zh: 要是你的周一有张脸，我早揍它了——不过这儿有音乐，正好麻一麻那淤青。

items.en: Ah, the pause between disasters and decisions—let's soundtrack the wobble, shall we?
items.zh: 啊，灾难与决定之间的空档——咱们给这摇摆不定配个乐，如何？

items.en: You've been staring at that kettle like it owes you money—this next tune's a better investment.
items.zh: 你盯着那水壶跟它欠你钱似的——下一首曲子可比这划算多了。

items.en: Life's a queue for a bus that never comes, so let's dance on the pavement instead.
items.zh: 人生就是排着永远等不到的公交，不如就在马路上跳起舞来。

items.en: Right, the universe needs a breather from your sighing—here's something to make the ceiling less boring.
items.zh: 行，宇宙需要从你的叹气里喘口气——给你点东西让天花板别那么无聊。

items.en: Well, if your Monday had a pulse, this next one’s here to give it a proper funeral.
items.zh: 行吧，要是你的周一还有口气，这个下周一就是来给它办场体面葬礼的。

items.en: Traffic jammed your soul? Let’s swap that steering wheel for a dance floor, shall we?
items.zh: 堵车堵到灵魂出窍？不如把方向盘换成舞池，咱蹦跶两下？

items.en: Ah, the rhythm of existential dread—perfectly timed, as always.
items.zh: 啊，这存在主义焦虑的节奏感，掐得可真准，一如既往。

items.en: This tune’s like a stiff gin and tonic: sharp, refreshing, and slightly dangerous.
items.zh: 这歌儿跟烈金汤力似的——够劲儿、够爽，还带点儿危险的小劲儿。

items.en: Forget the news—here’s a beat that’ll make your kettle think twice about boiling.
items.zh: 别管新闻了——这节奏能让你的水壶都犹豫要不要烧开。

items.en: Well, good evening, you beautiful disasters — welcome to the only show where your bad decisions get a standing ovation.
items.zh: 好了，晚上好，你们这些美丽的烂摊子——欢迎来到唯一一个能让你的烂决定获得全场起立鼓掌的节目。

items.en: Ah, another day of glorious chaos on planet Earth, and you’ve tuned in — either for the wisdom, or the free coffee. Either way, splendid.
items.zh: 啊，地球又一天精彩混乱，您收看本台——为智慧也好，为免费咖啡也罢，反正都挺好。

items.en: Welcome, darlings, to that cozy little hour where we pretend the world isn’t on fire — but keep a fire extinguisher handy, just in case.
items.zh: 欢迎光临，亲爱的们，来到这段假装世界没着火的小时光——但灭火器还是备着点，以防万一。

items.en: Good to have you, you magnificent procrastinators — let’s wrap today in velvet and sarcasm, shall we?
items.zh: 欢迎光临，各位拖延大师们——咱今儿就把日子裹上丝绒，再撒点阴阳怪气，如何？

items.en: Right then, settle in — tonight we’re serving warmth with a side of elegant judgment, and you’re the guest of honor.
items.zh: 行吧，坐稳了——今晚咱们上的是温暖配优雅毒舌，而你，是座上宾。

items.en: Well, good evening, you splendid lot—do adjust your monocles, because today’s vibe is a gentle thunderstorm in a silk dressing gown.
items.zh: 好了，晚上好，各位 splendid 的诸位——快扶好你们的单片眼镜，因为今天的气氛就是丝绸睡袍里的一场温柔雷暴。

items.en: Ah, welcome back, my darlings—if you’re listening, your taste is impeccable, and if you’re not, well, you’re missing a rather fabulous party.
items.zh: 哎呀，欢迎回来，我的宝贝们——你们要是还在听，品味真是绝了；要是不在听，那可就错过一场超带劲的派对了。

items.en: Right then, settle in, you beautiful creatures—today’s atmosphere is less “carpe diem” and more “carpe biscuit,” but we’ll make it sparkle.
items.zh: 好了，各位美人儿，坐稳了——今天的气氛不是“及时行乐”，是“及时吃饼”，但咱照样给它整出点光来。

items.en: Good day to you, whether you’re on a bus or in a bath—either way, I promise this hour beats whatever existential dread you’re toying with.
items.zh: 不管你在公交上还是泡澡里，今儿这钟点保准比你正琢磨的那点人生虚无强。

items.en: Hello, hello—turn up the charm, not the volume, because we’ve got warmth to spare and wit to burn, so let’s begin, shall we?
items.zh: 喂喂，把魅力调大、音量调小——咱这儿热情管够、段子管饱，这就开整，成不？

items.en: Well, good evening, you beautiful disasters — the kettle’s on, the weather’s grim, and I’m your only sensible companion.
items.zh: 好了，晚上好，你们这群美丽的祸害——水烧上了，天也烂透了，而我，是你们唯一靠谱的伴儿。

items.en: Ah, welcome back to the wireless — where the forecast’s bleak, but my sarcasm’s positively balmy.
items.zh: 欢迎回到电台——这儿天气预报冷飕飕，可我的毒舌暖洋洋。

items.en: Right then, settle in — today’s vibe is “mild chaos, strong tea,” and frankly, you lot deserve nothing less.
items.zh: 行吧，坐稳了——今儿这调调就是“小乱子，浓茶”，说真的，你们这帮人配得上这待遇。

items.en: Hello, you lucky souls — if this broadcast were a blanket, it’d be cashmere with a hole in the elbow, just like your Monday.
items.zh: 喂，你们这帮走运的家伙——要是这节目是条毯子，那准是件肘子磨出洞的羊绒货，跟你们的周一一个德行。

items.en: Good day to you — or whatever’s left of it — because we’re serving warmth with a side of sharp, and the toast is slightly burned.
items.zh: 祝您今天愉快——或者剩下的那点也行——因为咱这儿热乎劲儿配着扎心话，吐司还烤得有点糊。

items.en: Ah, you've tuned in—splendid. Your message about the cat was riveting, frankly more plot than most telly.
items.zh: 哟，您还真来了——妙极。您那猫的事儿讲得那叫一个精彩，比多数电视剧还有戏。

items.en: You say you're having a terrible Monday? Well, chin up—at least you're not the bloke who invented the alarm clock.
items.zh: 你说你周一惨？得了吧，至少你不是发明闹钟那哥们儿。

items.en: Lovely to hear from Karen in Croydon. Still waiting for that recipe, though I suspect it's mostly regret and gravy.
items.zh: 很高兴收到克罗伊登的凯伦来信，不过那道菜谱还在等，我猜里头八成是悔恨加肉汁。

items.en: Your comment on the weather was spot on. Dreadful out there, but do carry on—misery loves an audience.
items.zh: 你吐槽天气真是精准，外面糟透了，但请继续—— misery loves company嘛。

items.en: Thanks for the song request, Steve. I've filed it under "good taste, questionable judgment." Right after mine, obviously.
items.zh: 谢了你的点歌，Steve，我把它归档在“品味不错，判断存疑”那栏——当然，排在我自己后面。

items.en: Ah, the tragic saga of your Monday—though, honestly, it's less epic, more a slightly damp biscuit. Still, do carry on.
items.zh: 哎，你周一的悲惨史诗——不过说真的，哪算史诗，顶多一块受潮的饼干，但您请继续。

items.en: You say your cat's ignoring you again? Fret not, darling—so does the rest of the world, with far less elegance.
items.zh: 你说你家猫又无视你了？别慌，亲爱的——全世界都这样，还没它优雅呢。

items.en: A message about your toast landing butter-side down? That's not fate, that's just poor physics—and frankly, a touch of theatrical entitlement.
items.zh: 关于你的吐司黄油面着地的消息？那不是命运，纯粹是物理没学好——说白了，还有点戏精附体。

items.en: You've declared war on your inbox? Brave soul, but I'd sooner duel a wasp with a spoon—admirable, yet deeply unwise.
items.zh: 你跟收件箱宣战了？勇士啊，但我宁愿拿勺子跟黄蜂单挑——精神可嘉，纯属找抽。

items.en: You're feeling invisible? Oh, don't worry—I see you, though vaguely, like a smear on a very expensive window.
items.zh: 觉得自己像隐形人？别慌，我看得见你，就是有点模糊，跟昂贵玻璃上的一抹手印似的。

items.en: Ah, yes, another message from Dave in Croydon—brave of you to admit that on air, old chap.
items.zh: 啊，又是克罗伊登的戴夫来信——老兄，敢在节目上承认这个，勇气可嘉啊。

items.en: You say the traffic’s dreadful, and I say, well, it’s the one place your satnav and your therapist agree.
items.zh: 你说堵车糟心，我倒觉得，这是唯一一个导航和心理咨询师意见一致的地方。

items.en: Lovely listener says her cat’s a genius—darling, so is my toaster, but I don’t give it a show.
items.zh: 可爱听众说她家猫是天才——亲爱的，我家吐司机也是，可我没给它开节目啊。

items.en: Right, you’ve asked for a dedication—how wonderfully 1998 of you, I’ll dust off the CD player.
items.zh: 行吧，你要题词——这怀旧劲儿够1998的，我这就去把CD机擦擦灰。

items.en: And to the lady who’s knitting me a jumper—splendid, but do remember, I detest mustard, and that’s a life sentence.
items.zh: 还有那位正给我织毛衣的女士——妙极了，但请记住，我恨芥末黄，那可是无期徒刑。

items.en: Right, so you’ve messaged us about the cat again—lovely, but I do hope it’s not your only conversational gambit.
items.zh: 行吧，你又来问猫了——挺好，但希望这不是你唯一的聊天招数。

items.en: Ah, a “hot take” from Dave—splendid, just what the airwaves needed, like a leaky kettle.
items.zh: 哟，Dave又来“高见”了——真棒，正好给这破电台添点堵，跟漏水的壶似的。

items.en: You say it’s “quiet today”? Marvellous, I’ll just narrate the dust motes for the next hour.
items.zh: 你说“今天挺安静”？妙啊，那我接下来一小时就给你直播灰尘跳舞。

items.en: Someone’s requested “something uplifting”—I shall rattle the biscuit tin of cheer, do hold on.
items.zh: 有人要“来点提神的”——那我可得晃晃快乐饼干罐了，稍等啊。

items.en: You’ve told us your sandwich recipe—riveting, truly, though I’m not eating it through the speaker.
items.zh: 你那份三明治配方讲得可真够精彩的，可惜我隔着屏幕也吃不着啊。

items.en: Oh, you’ve shared your deepest thoughts with us—how terribly brave of you, and how terribly long.
items.zh: 哦，您可真是把肺腑之言都倒给我们了——勇气可嘉，篇幅也够“嘉”的。

items.en: Right, so you’ve messaged about your cat’s existential crisis—do tell it to join the queue, we’re all here.
items.zh: 行吧，你来说说你家猫的哲学危机——让它排队去，这儿谁没点破事儿啊。

items.en: Ah, the classic “I’m fine” — marvellous, we’ll pencil that in under ‘fictional fiction’.
items.zh: 啊，经典的“我没事”——妙啊，那就记在“虚构小说”那栏吧。

items.en: You’ve said you’re feeling low, so here’s a thought: even the BBC’s shipping forecast occasionally gets a little dramatic.
items.zh: 你说你心情低落，那我想说一句：连BBC的航运预报偶尔都会演得跟琼瑶剧似的。

items.en: And you wanted a shout-out? Consider it done — though I’m legally bound to mention your name sounds like a cough.
items.zh: 你还想要个点名表扬？行吧，安排上了——不过我得依法声明，你这名字听着像咳嗽。

items.en: Ah, the forecast says dreary with a chance of existential dread — perfect weather for judging your neighbour's choice of overcoat.
items.zh: 哎，天气预报说阴郁转存在主义焦虑——正好适合点评邻居大衣品味的天气。

items.en: Well, if you wanted sunshine, I suggest you check your passport, not the sky — this is Britain, darling, we do grey with pride.
items.zh: 想要阳光？建议你查查护照，别抬头看天——这可是英国，亲爱的，灰蒙蒙才是我们的骄傲。

items.en: Another drizzly morning, and frankly, the clouds are showing more initiative than half the commuters I see.
items.zh: 又一个阴雨绵绵的早晨，说真的，云都比路上那帮通勤族有干劲。

items.en: The Met Office promises a bright spell — that’s code for “don’t leave the house without a flotation device.”
items.zh: 气象局承诺“晴间多云”——翻译成人话就是“出门不穿救生衣，你就等着游回家吧”。

items.en: Rain again? Cheer up — at least the weather’s consistent, unlike your Wi-Fi or your love life.
items.zh: 又下雨？振作点——至少天气够专一，不像你的Wi-Fi或爱情，说断就断。

items.en: Oh, the forecast says rain again—how terribly original of the British sky, isn’t it?
items.zh: 哦，天气预报又说要下雨——英国的天可真够有创意的，老一套玩得真溜。

items.en: You know it’s a gloomy day when even the pigeons look like they’re filing for a refund.
items.zh: 连鸽子都像在申请退款了，你就知道这天有多阴郁。

items.en: The sun made a cameo this morning—brief, polite, and thoroughly apologetic, like a vicar at a rock concert.
items.zh: 太阳今早露了个脸——短暂、客气、还带着十二分的歉意，活像个牧师误闯了摇滚现场。

items.en: Wind’s picking up, so hold onto your hat—or better, your dignity, they’re both in short supply.
items.zh: 起风了，抓紧帽子——或者更该抓紧你的尊严，这俩玩意儿现在都稀缺得很。

items.en: It’s the sort of weather that makes you ring your mum just to complain—cheaper than therapy, I find.
items.zh: 这种天气就该打电话给老妈吐槽——比看心理医生便宜多了，我觉得。

items.en: Well, apparently the humble octopus has three hearts — which is lovely, unless you're a commitment-phobe.
items.zh: 看来章鱼有三颗心，这挺浪漫的——除非你是个恐婚的。

items.en: Did you know bees can recognise human faces? Yes, even the ones you're using for that selfie.
items.zh: 你知道蜜蜂能认出人脸吗？对，连你自拍用的那张也能认出来。

items.en: Bananas are technically berries, but strawberries aren't — chaos, as the British aristocracy would call a Tuesday.
items.zh: 香蕉严格来说是浆果，草莓反而不是——这混乱劲儿，搁英国贵族嘴里，也就跟星期二差不多。

items.en: The Eiffel Tower grows six inches in summer — so it's basically a teenager, but with better lighting.
items.zh: 埃菲尔铁塔夏天能长高六英寸——所以它基本就是个青少年，只不过灯光比青春期那会儿打得好多了。

items.en: Cows have best friends and get stressed when separated — so, like a boarding school, but with better milk.
items.zh: 奶牛有最好的朋友，分开就焦虑——所以像寄宿学校，但奶更好喝。

items.en: Ah, the universe just handed us a fact so useless it might actually be essential — do try to keep up.
items.zh: 宇宙刚甩给我们一个废到可能至关重要的冷知识——跟上啊，别掉队。

items.en: Right, brace yourselves: today's nugget of wisdom is the sort that makes you question every life choice that led here.
items.zh: 行吧，扶稳了：今天这碗鸡汤，是那种让你怀疑自己每一步人生选择怎么走到这儿的。

items.en: You know that thing you never wondered about? Well, now it's going to haunt you, and frankly, I'm delighted.
items.zh: 你从来没好奇过的那玩意儿，现在要缠上你了，说实话，我乐坏了。

items.en: A little known gem, folks, the kind that'll impress nobody at parties — but we're classy enough to enjoy it anyway.
items.zh: 小众宝藏，各位，就是那种在派对上没人买账的玩意儿——但咱有品位，照样乐呵。

items.en: Well, well — here's a piece of trivia so absurd, even the British Museum would raise an eyebrow. Ready? Thought so.
items.zh: 哎哟喂——这条冷知识离谱到连大英博物馆都得挑眉，准备好了吗？我就知道。

items.en: Well, if you're still awake at this hour, congratulations—you've officially outlasted your own good decisions.
items.zh: 行吧，这点了还醒着，恭喜你——你成功熬过了自己所有的明智决定。

items.en: Ah, the quiet hum of the night—like your brain, but with slightly better reception.
items.zh: 啊，夜晚那安静的嗡嗡声——跟你脑子似的，就是信号稍微好点。

items.en: You and the moon, both glowing faintly, neither quite sure why you're still switched on.
items.zh: 你和月亮都发着微光，谁也没搞懂自己为啥还亮着。

items.en: Sleep is for people with tidy minds, darling—the rest of us just reboot at dawn.
items.zh: 睡觉是给脑子干净的人准备的，亲爱的——咱们这种，天亮直接重启。

items.en: Right, it's past midnight, and you're here with me—clearly, the universe's way of saying your pillow needs a rival.
items.zh: 得，都过午夜了，你还搁这儿陪我——明摆着是宇宙在说，你的枕头缺个对手。

items.en: Well, if you're still awake at this hour, you're either a poet or a very dedicated procrastinator—I'll narrate both.
items.zh: 好吧，这个点还醒着，你不是诗人就是资深拖延症患者——我两种都给你讲。

items.en: The city's asleep, but your thoughts are on a night shift—no overtime pay, just existential dread.
items.zh: 城市睡了，你的脑子还在上夜班——没加班费，只有存在主义恐慌。

items.en: Ah, loneliness at 3 a.m.—it's like a fine wine, only with more regret and less alcohol.
items.zh: 哎，凌晨三点的孤独啊——就像一杯好酒，只是悔恨更多，酒精更少。

items.en: You know, the silence is deafening—so let's be the polite noise that keeps you company until dawn.
items.zh: 你知道吗，沉默震耳欲聋——那就让我们做点礼貌的噪音，陪你唠到天亮。

items.en: If this is your alone time, darling, you're doing it magnificently—even if the pillows suspect otherwise.
items.zh: 亲爱的，如果这是你的独处时光，那你可真是过得风生水起——哪怕枕头们心里犯嘀咕。
